articleTitle: Analysis of Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) of UAV Operators
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become common in civil and defense environments. Due to growing accident rates relative to human flight operations. The demand for qualified UAV operators is increasing as well as clear and standard legislation. Many factors have a severe impact on the availability and usability of UAVs. A well-known method for assessing the risk of accidents causation is the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), which breaks down the causes of accidents into four main categories: (i) organizational influences, (ii) supervision, (iii) preconditions, and (iv) acts. In this study, a unique approach that combines the HFACS model with an analytical hierarchal process (AHP) decision-making model is presented. A questionnaire has been created for this study’s investigation of the crucial aspects of accidents as seen by UAV operators.

articleTitle: Analysis of the introduction of artificial intelligence in the control of UAV
abstract: Recently, the demand for unmanned aerial vehicles has been growing at an exponential rate and unmanned aerial vehicles are being used in many industries for many purposes. By adding artificial intelligence, the potential of these devices increases. Artificial intelligence itself can make operation of unmanned aircraft easier and more efficient, but it does not have only positive aspects. Artificial intelligence in drones requires more energy and also much more computing power. The paper is focused on the analysis of the introduction of artificial intelligence in the control of unmanned aerial vehicles. The paper contains comparative analysis of scientific papers that are dealing with artificial intelligence in the control of unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Correcting surface errors of the scanned gyroplane 3D model using Siemens NX software
abstract: This paper deals with the correction of surface errors in a scanned model of a gyroplane which is the subject of the IMAF (Innovative measurement of airspeed of unconventional flying vehicles) project.Nowadays, advanced technologies are an important aspect of developing and advancing new technologies. Technologies play a huge role in the advancement of manufacturing, it should be noted that first and foremost such technologies are aimed at product development and improvement.In some cases, when creating a 3D model, you should not follow the standard path, gradually creating a CAD model. Sometimes it is more rational to use 3D scanning methods and only then, with the help of reverse engineering, reach the CAD model. Creating a CAD model in this way comes with some problems. One of them is surface defects that occur during the scanning process.The article discusses a practical solution to this problem. Using the available functions of the Siemens NX software, we processed the model from surface defects such as bumps, ledges, and depressions.

articleTitle: Selected Aspects of the Aircraft Selection and Evaluation Process for an Airline
abstract: In this paper, the problem of optimizing the process of aircraft selection and evaluation was addressed with emphasis on the procedure of optimal aircraft selection for the needs of an airline using the developed algorithms. At the beginning of the paper, an analysis of selected models for optimizing the selection of aircraft equipment for an airline is carried out. Further, the basic criteria that are most used in the decision-making process concerning aircraft selection have been identified. Based on this, the different types of aircraft that are mostly used by airlines for short, medium to medium-long haul routes have been identified. Furthermore, algorithms for airline aircraft selection were developed. A simulation of the coverage of the market requirements for passenger transportation at the five hub airports used by the generated airline was created.

articleTitle: Use of IoT in Air Transport
abstract: This paper deals with the topic analysis of the use of IoT in air transport. The paper consists of several parts in which authors gradually focus on the technology of the Internet of Things, what are the advantages and disadvantages of this smart technology, on what principle it works and the introduction of the technology into practice. This paper is focused on how the individual airlines approached implementation of IoT into everyday life. Authors also focused on different ways of using IoT technology at airports, giving specific examples of how they are using IoT technology, what results they expect by the use of smart technology. Subsequently, authors focused on the analysis, using cluster analysis to which the data are applied, while trying to find the relationship between IoT technology and services on airports.

articleTitle: Inspection of wind power plant turbines by using UAV
abstract: The paper introduces the types of wind power plants’ turbines, the possibilities of their inspections, the examination of the blades, the necessary tools and devices and the UAV used during the examinations. The complete procedure of the in-situ examination is described, and the picture processing is also shown here. As a conclusion it can be said that the blade status of the wind turbines basically determinates the safety energy production and the efficiency of the power plants.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Introducing new Standard Arrival and Departures Routes at Malacky Airport
abstract: The topic of the article is devoted to air traffic services routes for the effective use of the selected Slovak airspace and the elimination of negative impacts of aviation activity on the environment and public health. The main goal of the article is to analyze the current state of standard departure and arrival routes at Malacky Airport, to describe the factors affecting standard arrival and departure routes and individual types of approaches with regard to wake turbulence, weather, noise and the human factor, to analyze software tools for creating standard arrival and departure routes departure routes at a selected airport in the Slovak Republic with an emphasis on safety and risk assessment in air traffic control.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Risks Assessment of selected EUROCONTROL’s surveillance products
abstract: Cybersecurity is without doubt becoming a societal challenge. It even starts to affect sectors that were not considered to be at risk in the past because of their relative isolation. One of these sectors is aviation in general, and specifically air traffic management. Nowadays, the cyber security is one of the essential issues of current Air Traffic Systems. Compliance with the basic principles of cyber security is mandated by European Union law as well as the national law. Therefore, EUROCONTROL as the provider of several tools or services (ARTAS, EAD, SDDS, etc.), is regularly conducting various activities, such as the cyber-security assessments, penetration testing, supply chain risk assessment, in order to maintain and improve persistence of the products against the cyber-attacks.

articleTitle: Drones for Monitoring of Aeras and Objects
abstract: The presented article deals with the utilization possibility of drones as a part of the system for the monitoring of the area of interest with the primary goal of protecting the vulnerable group of people against the spread of viral diseases located in the protected objects or areas or on the contrary, to monitor buildings or objects with the infected or ill people. The article presents the most critical aspects of implementing the proposed concept together with the main identified risks and utilization possibilities of the module for epidemics as a part of the constructive simulation software.

articleTitle: Generative Design in the Construction of the Modern Sensor Attachments
abstract: The process of designing components for the aerospace industry, combined with the computing power of modern computers, which can handle many simulations, offers designers entirely new possibilities for model creation, which often go beyond conventional manufacturing possibilities. Generative design thus opens completely innovative design concepts, as it creates unique and innovative solutions inspired by nature. Considering this it can be concluded that the development of this modern design approach has the possibility of a significant change in the way designs are created. This change would not be possible without the development of modern manufacturing technologies, such as additive manufacturing. These modern production processes are gradually becoming a part of the design of many components not only in the aviation industry. This article presents the utilization possibility of the 3D printing in the design and manufacturing of the attachment of the sensors with the emphasis on the optimization of the model from the material consumption and the production time point of view.

articleTitle: Analysis of Codes of Ethics in the Transport and Logistics Industry in the Czech Republic
abstract: The demands being placed by stakeholders on businesses with regards to ethical behaviour and conduct have been growing on a long-term basis. Within this context, a code of ethics is considered the most important tool of ethical management in companies. This applies to an even greater extent within the field of transport and logistics due to the nature of the business. This contribution therefore sets out to analyse codes of ethics in companies operating in the transport and logistics industry in the Czech Republic. Two research questions were formulated in compliance with the goal. The first sought to determine the quality of the codes of ethics of companies operating within the industry. The second sought to determine to what extent the contents of those documents met preconditions for efficacy. A qualitative comparative analysis of 21 codes of ethics was used to obtain the answers to the formulated research questions. The results of the analysis showed that significant differences exist between the examined documents in relation to their quality and contents. In terms of the provisions that form the preconditions for the efficacy of these documents, it was found that significant improvements were required in a substantial number and parts of the examined documents.

articleTitle: Optimization of Legislative Requirements for Heavy Equipment of Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting Brigade
abstract: The airport and in its surroundings is a necessary condition for maintaining high air traffic safety. For this purpose, airports establish their own Fire Brigades. The article analyses in detail the regulations and documents related to the mandatory provision of rescue equipment at airports in case of an air accident or incident. These are exclusively ICAO Annex 14 and the adopted document L14. Based on the analysis, shortcomings were identified in terms of the required equipment, where the regulations only provide for fire and aircraft extrication. This result was found to be insufficient as there are other threats in air traffic which are not mentioned in the current legislation and the Fire Brigades must rely on their previous experience or the experience of other brigades in the world. The model airport V. H. Prague, where we performed a comprehensive verification of rescue equipment in relation to the regulatory base, demonstrated a significantly higher level of equipment than prescribed by the current legislation. This has led to the development of several general recommendations for the provision of rescue equipment to cover hitherto neglected risks. As part of the recommendation process, sub-parameters of airports were considered to increase efficiency. If some of these recommendations can be implemented in future legislation, the ways in which the Fire and Rescue Service can deal with emergencies will be developed and thus the safety of the whole system will be improved.

articleTitle: Relationship between Air Transport and the Economic Growth
abstract: There is a close interaction between air transport and the economy. The growth of economic activity over the last few decades has resulted in the enormous development of air transport. Air transport is a factor, but also an indicator of its development. The aim of the paper is to discuss the interaction between air transport and the state economy and to analyze and point out the relationship between air transport and the growth of gross domestic product (GDP) using the correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Relation between wing aspect ratio and induced drag
abstract: In the work, was presented problem of drag, which occur during the flight of aircraft, and two types of wings were compared in terms of the induced drag produced. Following drag was described successively: friction, shape, interference and induced, the conditions under which they arise and how they can be counteracted. Then, the focus was on induced drag, all the ways to minimize it were presented, such as: the use of aerodynamic combs, increasing the wing aspect ratio and the use of wingtip modifications. The types of tips and solutions used by aviation manufacturers were described in detail. A comparative study of two types of Aero AT-3 wings was carried out, and they were subjected to computer simulation in order to determine the difference in the induced drag produced. The results clearly show that in the case studied, increasing the wing aspect ratio has greater importance in reducing the induced drag than the use of a winglet. The use of a modified wing allows to reduce this drag by more than 20%.

articleTitle: Methodology for Inspecting the Correctness of the Function of Airport Lighting Systems Using a Commercially Available UAS
abstract: This paper deals with the use of unmanned aircraft systems for inspecting the correctness of the function of airport lighting systems. These days, inspections are typically done using so-called flying labs, but unmanned aircraft systems are showing that they can be significantly more effective in these tasks. In this paper, commercially available unmanned aircraft systems were used for the inspection of lighting systems at the small uncontrolled airport Vysoké Mýto. The inspection results in an acceptable accuracy of it, which leads to the possibility of significant savings for this task in the future.

articleTitle: Use of Computer Simulation to Optimize UAV Swarm Flying
abstract: Nowadays, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles are only being utilized in a limited number of sectors, such as agriculture, cinematography, photogrammetry, or research. The implementation of formation flight could greatly enhance the applicability and make the UAVs operate more effectively. This paper analyses the contemporary state of implementation of UAVs in conditions of their flight in formations, mechanisms by which the formations are coordinated and proposes their further use in the future. We also analyse the possibilities and use cases of development of technology applicable for coordination of multiple UAVs flying in formations. Furthermore, we discuss implementation of advanced mission planning and swarming software, on the usage of specifically chosen hardware and structural components for construction of advanced UAVs capable of coordinated flight in formations or swarms. These formations are configurable to take form of various shapes dependent of the particular application demanded by the operator. For instance, UAV formations could be greatly utilized by delivery companies, for search and rescue purposes or intra city medical material transport between hospitals. All analyses, data collection, monitoring and control are done virtually. This methodology serves to optimalization the swarm flying, without the need of real experimental flights.

articleTitle: Determining the Break Even Point of the Air Carrier
abstract: In this contribution, the problems of revenue management and the break even point of the air carrier determination are solved. The main goal is to develop a procedure to determine the break even point of the air carrier with a focus on covering operating costs for the specified lines. An airline cost model has been created for the operation of the Košice - Bratislava route using the A319 aircraft. A computer program has been also made where the ticket prices can be randomly or manually loaded along with the number of tickets sold at a given price. The break even point for a specific reference example has been determined by simulation.

articleTitle: Actual costs of equity in Transportation and storage
abstract: The paper deals with the actual costs of equity in the sector NACE “H” (transportation and storage). The paid-out profit shares, expressed through changes in the retained earnings of previous years and the profit or loss for the current accounting period, will be considered as actual incurred costs. The input data will be obtained from the Cribis / Albertina database and will be based on the earnings in the transport sector for the period 2016–2020. As the research sample, only active and profitable companies will be selected. Subsequently, 5 categories will be created according to the volume of sales. The results show that the COVID-19 pandemic has affected the transport sector, except for Category 4 with a turnover of CZK 100,0, 000 to CZK 1,000,000,000, in which both retained earnings from previous years and the profit for the current accounting period grew. Regarding the share of retained earnings from past years in the earnings of the current accounting period, category 4 shows the sharpest decrease. The average percentage in each category was 82%.

Author Keywords: Current earnings for the current accounting period

articleTitle: Laser Attacks on Aircraft and Some Experiences from the Czech Republic
abstract: The article deals with the issue of laser attacks directed at aircraft, the incidence of which has been increasing in recent years. Evidence from past events points to the considerable danger of this criminal activity, which can lead to an accident with fatal consequences. This article refers to the recent laser attack that happened near Václav Havel International Airport in Prague. In the discussion, the authors then reflect on the possible risks associated with these attacks and also on how to prevent these incidents.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sustainable Aviation Fuels Market
abstract: For decades now, aviation industry was looking for possibilities of reduction of greenhouse gas emissions of the sector. Sustainable aviation fuels are seen as one of the most viable paths. This study presents the analysis of the current state of sustainable aviation fuels market. It focuses on the SAF place on the aviation fuels market and its potential to compete and in the future replace conventional fossil fuels. In the introduction we present sustainable aviation fuels, their production pathways, characteristics, and potential as a green technology to contribute to greenhouse gas emission reduction. In the next parts, the paper focuses on the market analysis, as well as analysis of the SAF prices and their potential competitiveness on the market. In the final parts, paper present next steps necessary to secure SAF wider implementation.

articleTitle: The volume of freight transport in V4 countries relative to GDP
abstract: In the contribution, we deal with the development of GDP on the volume of transported goods in the V4 countries with regard to the post-Covid and pre-Covid periods. As part of the research, we examined the development of the period from 2011 to 2020, for which annual data were available. We assume that despite the critical years with regard to COVID-19, except for a minor period of decline or stagnation, the volume of transport itself is relatively stable. As part of the examination of the selected countries, it is significant that some countries from the V4 experienced a sharp increase in transport at the end of the given period, which ultimately had an impact on the GDP of the given country.

articleTitle: Modern Technologies & Human Performance Taxonomy in Air Traffic Management Development. Polish and Georgian Case Studies
abstract: The Global Air Navigation Plan (GANP) is a flexible global engineering approach that allows all States to advance their Air Navigation capacities based on their specific operational requirements. One of the most important problematic part for successful implementation of the GANP is innovative air traffic management system and aircraft on-board technologies effective interrelationship taking into consideration human factors.The research work is focused on the creation of methodology for comparison gap between Air Traffic Management (ATM), aircraft modern on-board systems and aviation professionals competencies. One of the problem in the implementation of the new technologies is that, there are currently no unified requirements for all categories of ATM, and on the other hand, the development of modern trends requires new competencies from operational and maintenance personnel. This problems becomes even more noticeable in countries that have just started an active modernization of ATM systems.This paper examines the expertise of human performance specialists and the tools they use have been recognized as key ingredients to advance ATM infrastructures in the process of modernizing the national air traffic control systems. Research oriented to the Polish and Georgian case studies, as in both counties quickly improves the ATM technologies the development of personnel skills is critical. As a result taxonomy of key human performance issues for the design and integration of large-scale future ATM programs is proposed.

articleTitle: The Concept of Financing the Preparatory Phase of an Airline – Airline Maker
abstract: Starting an airline business is very difficult especially in such a competitive environment as aviation. During the preparatory phase of an airline, it is necessary to hire a top team of experts, prepare several business analysis, process a quantity of plans, manuals, and handbooks, start the procurement process of airplane/s or go through certification. The total costs of the preparatory phase depend on several aspects, such as the type and strategy of the airline or method of procurement of the airplane/s, but it starts from hundreds of thousands of euros. Of course, there are several models, thanks to which you can get a potential investor, but they all have something in common. You need to have at least a detailed and realistic business plan, which you cannot prepare without analysis and an experienced team. The aim of this paper is to propose a financing concept for the preparatory phase of the airline company Suljets.

articleTitle: Design of Mirror System for Visual Illusion Induction
abstract: Negative factors affecting the flight safety need to be counteracted by measures based on an understanding of the nature of the problem. Due to the fact that visual illusions are considered a factor capable of endangering the safety of the crew and passengers, it is necessary to understand the mechanics of their creation. Therefore, this paper focuses on the device able to induce specific visual illusion by the means of moving perspective that could be used as a support during the efforts to understand the mechanism of such illusions. The mirror system with variable speed of movement is designed to induce a change of perspective and thus postural destabilization of the subject. Proposed device was tested in the experiment involving postural stability measurements in the form of centre of pressure monitoring using the balance board as the indicators of sucesfull illusion induction. The results does not confirm the ilussion induction. However, the effect of mirror movement direction is observed.

articleTitle: Buffer zones for forced engine-out landing in ultra-light aircraft operation
abstract: This article researches buffer zones for engine-out operation of the ultra-light aircraft Viper SD-4. The danger areas are estimated by taking into account the average flown routes and the profile of the flight. Considering the trajectory and the elevation profile together with glide ratio we can estimate the buffer zones. Buffer zones are covering radius of possible emergency landing areas. Using high resolution satellite images, aerial photos and GIS tools enables to estimate such zones. Within the buffer zone the flight crew is capable of gliding and performing the emergency landing. With increasing height, the size of buffer zone expands proportionally. The meteorological conditions were not considered by estimating the radius of a buffer zone. This analysis of GIS and GPS data could potentially increase the safety of the flights along preselected routes even outside of the aerodrome control zone.

articleTitle: Development of road infrastructure in the Slovak Republic
abstract: The road infrastructure of each state tells about many facts that can be linked to progress and financing in that country. The road infrastructure is often one of the main conditions for the entry of new investors into the country, because it is the roads that facilitate not only the transportation of people, but also goods and components that affect the entire production process. Therefore, road infrastructure can be seen as an indicator of the development of a state or a smaller territorial unit. However, it is not only its length, but of course also its quality, that is why the presented article deals with the current situation in Slovakia, while analyzing the state’s current approach to the given issue in more detail, and at the same time indicates the development in this area within the strategic documents.

articleTitle: Synchronization of time bases and its effect on the accuracy of determining the position of flying objects
abstract: The article analyzes the issue of determining the location of flying objects that functions in the aviation communication network. We verify the architecture of the proposed models on the created computer model. We performed the simulations in the Matlab program environment. In the article, we present the determined parameters for the accuracy of determining position flight object based on information from users of the aviation communication network. The performed simulation analyzes the errors that naturally occur during the real operation of the communication network so that each user is artificially burdened with the error produced by the selected random number generator. This Generator generates the so-called pseudo-random errors that represent the instability of the time synchronization of individual users in the communication network.

articleTitle: Air Policing in V-4 countries
abstract: The article clarifies Air Policing as a system for ensuring safety in the airspace. The introductory part explains the basic concepts, which are crucial for proper understanding of Air Policing mission. Further sections clarify the legislative apparatus and briefly describe the structure of the forces of the means that carry out Air Poling’s tasks. This is followed by introduction of the basic levels of possible cooperation of the V-4 countries in the performance of Air Policing’s tasks. The last section briefly assess of the basic advantages and disadvantages of each proposal.

articleTitle: Movement Analysis of the Aircraft Optoelectronic Tracking System in Lateral Plane
abstract: The paper describes the analysis of the movement transformation of the tracking optoelectronic system of a fast aircraft. The transformation is performed in the selected phase of flight in the lateral planes. The mathematical model of the aircraft was extended by an optoelectronic tracking system model and a weapon movement model. Mathematical models of the proposed integrated system are described by transfer functions, which are transferred to the state space with evaluation in the simulation environment. Control of the automatic tracking system on the aircraft was designed with the ability to control the tracking line on the selected tracking object in order to reduce the impact of the error in the dynamics of the aircraft movement, the movement of the monitored object and the optoelectronic tracking system. The laws of control of the optoelectronic system and the aircraft have been defined. The optimization of the proposed methods was realized under changing flight conditions of the aircraft and the tracking object as optimal gains. Optimal gains are determined by the values given in the difference speed and altitude for aircraft flight.

articleTitle: The Potential of Selected Industry 4.0 Tools in the Aerospace Industry
abstract: The article deals with selected technological tools of the Industry 4.0 concept and the possibilities of their use and implementation within the aviation industry. In the introduction, the authors discuss the current state of the issue and individual selected tools. In the second chapter, they differentiate the individual subsystems of virtual reality and the virtual environment in general as a useful tool of the Industry 4.0 concept, where emphasis is also placed on possible health complications within their use. In the third chapter, the authors present additive manufacturing as a possibility for the potential implementation of these tools. The conclusion of the article presents a summary of the facts found and pointing out the questions that need to be dealt with in the framework of further research on the given issue.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review on Aviation Operator’s Total Loads
abstract: In the aviation environment and air transport operations, safety is the most crucial element of the system; maintaining safe aeronautical operations is highly dependent on the aviation operators’ actions and reactions. Cognitive loads reflect the human contribution to the system; mental, communication, information, task, and workload shape the aviation total loads. The number of aviation accidents and incidents caused by human factors increases rapidly due to intensive technology and automation in aviation. Such recent examples of human-contributed aviation accidents can be given like (i) Casa 212-200, N497CA Flight accident, (ii) Ethiopian Airlines, ET-343 flight accident. Many previous studies focused on measuring the total load of pilots and ATCOs through different processes and flight scenarios using multiple sensors & devices. This paper reviews a variety of experimental studies differentiating the methodologies, scope, and outcomes. Eventually, the paper introduces a compromised and novel approach for measuring aviation operator loads in multiple scenarios.

articleTitle: Application Software of Modular System for Magnetic Characteristics Measurement
abstract: Nanosatellites’ stabilisation and attitude control are often discussed with the current trend of increasing space activities. Out of the many available technical solutions, a magnetorquer is an effective option for required torque generation. This type of electromagnetic actuator is preferred due to its relatively low weight, absence of moving parts, absence of propellants, simple construction, and relatively low production costs. In applications where fast reaction times are required, magnetorquers with a ferromagnetic core are primarily used. However, the performance of this type of magnetorquer is conditioned mainly by the magnetic properties of its ferromagnetic core. Therefore, a measurement system was developed to determine the magnetic characteristic of the open-end ferromagnetic samples. The advantage of this measuring system is its modular design, which enables a simple replacement of individual functional components to optimise the measuring process. Since systematic management of the measuring process is necessary for achieving effective operability of the measurement system, the application software with an integrated user interface was designed. Accordingly, the developed application software aims to control and configure the measuring process in pursuance of various input requirements, which makes prerequisites for the measurement system to be also used in the design of ferromagnetic cores of magnetometric probes intended for axial magnetic field measurement. The specific features and capabilities of the application software, considering its structure and programmed algorithms, are stated in this article.

articleTitle: Aviation Regulations for Drone Operations in the Slovak Republic and the EU
abstract: Drone technology provides a plenty of benefits and opportunities in a vast range of daily tasks. It is evident that we have a very exciting period for Slovak and EU’s drone operations sector. Nowadays, drones are used for recreational purposes, emergency services, police patrolling, media coverages, agricultural and environmental monitoring, security setups, and others. The popularity of drones indicates that the future of aviation will be inseparably confronted with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV). We witness an extensive application of drones that is opening new concerns regarding safety of their operations as well as ethics and morality of people. A protection of individual people rights, and orderly operated airspace, surely require to set a clear and effective legal framework in a respective country. This study deals with legal aspects of drone operations. The aim of this study is focus on how drones are legally bound in the legislation of the European Union and the Slovak Republic. This study presents a few overall objectives which will particularly contribute to secure safe drone operations. Also, the study suggests to use the risk-based concept as an appropriate decision making tool of lawmaking bodies. The applied method in this study was valid legal acts analysis. The study proves that governments must put enough attention to set out the framework for the safe operations of drones in the European skies.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study: Language Proficiency Requirements for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Aircraft Technicians
abstract: Aviation English is used by different aviation personnel besides air traffic controllers and pilots. However, the ICAO language proficiency requirements are designed only for pilot-air traffic controller communications, addressing solely the listening and speaking skills. The goal of these requirements is to limit misunderstandings in the course of flight by bringing the knowledge of all pilots and air traffic controllers to an acceptable level. This article focuses on the comparison of the English language requirements posed on aircraft technicians as opposed to pilots and air traffic controllers. ICAO language proficiency requirements provided a beginning in recognizing the significance of the English language, but there is a need for further development of language proficiency requirements dedicated to aircraft maintenance technicians, as their job requires them to read and understand English texts. The aircraft maintenance manuals, service bulletins, and other documentation provide instructions that have to be closely followed to ensure safety. The need for English proficiency in aircraft maintenance is acknowledged, however, there is still a need for guidance on the language requirements.

articleTitle: Unmanned aircraft (drones) as a security threat to the exercise of judicial power in the Slovak Republic
abstract: The article presents possible issues related to the security threat to the exercise of judicial power and violations of legislation related to unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operation. It describes the commercial and non-commercial rules for the use of UAVs. It also summarizes conditions regarding UAV weight, personnel and certification procedures, and the space where UAVs can conduct flight operations.

articleTitle: Empirical Pre-survey of Student - Pilots’ Opinions on the Evaluation Information System
abstract: The article presents the results of empirical pre-research of the opinions of students - pilots within the framework of the preparation of a questionnaire and the creation of a software tool for the comprehensive evaluation of the performance of students - pilots of the Faculty of Aviation of the Technical University in Košice in studies and flight training, for the improvement of individual study advice. The use of the method of questionnaire, analysis, deduction, and synthesis of knowledge made it possible to verify the answers to research questions. The pre-research was carried out on a smaller sample of students – pilots, who are, however, from the target group of the Faculty of Aviation of the Technical University in Košice. The results of the pre-research confirmed that the answering instructions are understandable, the questions are formulated and understandable to the report, the questionnaire items are logically arranged, and the questionnaire is sufficiently motivating. Errors that appeared during the pilot testing of the questionnaire were eliminated. The content of the pre-research also preliminarily confirmed the need for an innovative solution to the issue of comprehensive evaluation of the performance of students – pilots, with the support of information technology.

articleTitle: Risks determination during the life-cycle of conventional and sustainable aviation fuels - the environmental aspect
abstract: The paper is devoted to determining and analysing potential risks related to the production and use of conventional and sustainable jet fuels. The modern state in the sphere of sustainable aviation development and decreasing the negative impact of air transport on the environment is presented. The use of alternative jet fuels is shown as one of the most reliable solutions for the decarbonisation of aviation. For the purpose of the study, the stages of the fuel life cycle were proposed and considered. Risks were determined and classified according to the proposed stages. Environmental risks, which may occur during the direct use of conventional and alternative jet fuels, are discussed in detail with a focus on exhaust gas emissions. It is shown that both types of fuels present environmental danger on a local and global level. At the same time, due to the natural origin and specific composition, sustainable aviation fuels may have fewer environmental risks for human health, the environment and global decarbonisation initiatives. The fulfilled study provides fundamentals for the following research in the field of environmental risk assessment with the development of quantitative estimates and proposals of certain measures.

articleTitle: Air Accident Investigation and State Safety Oversight with CAST Analysis
abstract: Accidents and incidents bring to the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) necessary data to understand the current level of safety in the state. Their investigation is carried out by the safety investigation authority capable to perform independent investigation activities in the state or authorized organizations. The final reports often include safety recommendations that the organization or CAA should apply in the form of corrective actions. Since most accidents are the result of several causal factors, there is an opportunity to investigate occurrences using a systemic approach to safety. One of the methods that can be used to identify system safety issues is STAMP-based Casual Analysis based on Systems Theory (CAST). The full application of the CAST at the state level requires some changes in the processing of safety data today. The goal of this paper was to create a concept of using data for the investigation of air accidents with the CAST analysis. Then to study the usability of the CAST to process safety data at the state level, primarily under the state oversight of the Czech Republic. The proposed concept presented with marked components of the CAST and the necessary data and information for the investigation according to this methodology. The concept shows where changes would need to be made to the current system setting to use the CAST at the state level without limitations.

Author Keywords: Casual Analysis Based on Systems Theory

articleTitle: Analysis of The Most Critical Phase of the Flight Based on HRV Measurements of Pilots Workload
abstract: Constant changes and development of cockpit ergonomics can cause increased workload that can negatively affect pilot performance and jeopardize overall flight safety. This paper deals with comparing pilot workload during the flight on simulators with different cockpit ergonomics. The manuscript is focused on the flight phase during which the pilot showed the highest workload based on the Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measurement. The measurements participated in group of pilots who gradually flew the Instrument Landing System (ILS) final approach for runway 06 at the Zilina airport on the two different flight simulators with analog instruments and glass cockpit. The analysis compared the Parasympathetic Nervous System (PNS) and Sympathetic Nervous System (SNS) index during flight. The results showed the highest pilots’ workload during landing. The conclusions of the research point to the possibilities of using HRV measurements in the process of pilot training, but also to the general monitoring of the workload of aviation personnel. It is the research of the human factor that represents a large space for increasing the safety in aviation, which proves the topicality of research.

Index Terms: Changes In The Autonomic Nervous System

articleTitle: Evaluation of transport company financial situation
abstract: Monitoring financial health is crucial for any company because it can assess its financial stability. The aim of this contribution is to evaluate the financial health of the transport company BV Spedice s.r.o. The paper includes an analysis of financial statements—the balance sheet and profit and loss statement—for the period from 2010 to 2020. Analysis of ratios and vertical analysis of the balance sheet were performed. The company can be assessed as relatively stable, there was a significant decrease in profit during the years 2016 – 2019. However, the company responded well to the situation, it maintained a positive attitude towards the downturn and handled the crisis period well.

articleTitle: The Impact of Covid-19 on Marketing Mix and Economics of Airlines
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to assess the impact of covid-19 on marketing practices and airlines’ adaptation to the new business and economic environment. In the first part, we introduce a marketing mix framework and look at the impact of covid-19 on seat capacity and airline operating revenues. In the second part, we determine current marketing strategies using the marketing framework of the 4Ps and its impact on operational changes among full-service network carriers and low-cost carriers. The central theme in advertising and campaigns for full-service network carriers is high hygiene standards and cleanliness of flights, as passengers are concerned with not contracting covid-19 or other viruses during the longer flight routes. Low-cost carriers still focus primarily on the price and convenience to potential customers. Both types of carriers do improve and push out technology changes in terms of mobile apps, improved online check-ins and contactless, touchless kiosks used for airport check-ins. These slight changes increase passengers’ comfort, speed up the check-in process and minimize the spread of any viruses.

articleTitle: Aircraft Gas Turbine Engine Vibration Diagnostic Method
abstract: Airspace engineering, in its multidisciplinary content, uses various diagnostic methods aimed at the health monitoring of flying vehicle components. The paper is focused on the vibration diagnostic method. Authors have realized vibration measurements on gas turbine engine GTD-5M as preliminary research experiments made before vibration monitoring of aircraft gas turbine engines (AGTE). A purposefully focused processing method of the signal from the accelerometer has been developed. Multidisciplinary knowledge and experiences have been needed for measurement setup, analysis tools, and data interpretation. Cooperation of avionic specialists with engine technicians allowed to avoid long time study of signal recording and processing methods. The paper is focused on signal processing introductory for airspace engineers and technical personnel that deal with rotating machines’ vibrations. The basic theory comes from well-known authors – Randall (Australia), Cempel (Poland), Haris (UK), Doroshko (Russia) and Tuma (Czech rep.); however, they are not cited in all details. Their knowledge and experiences are often transformed by specialists who bring new findings in methodology, including authors of actual paper. Some complicated details cited are recommended to be studied deeply in original works.

articleTitle: Virtual Tower and its Practical Applications for Small Airports
abstract: In this paper, the possibilities of using small airports for air transport of passengers and cargo are presented. Emphasis is placed on air traffic management at small airports. As one of the possible alternatives for air traffic management at small airports we present the use of virtual tower, which allows to significantly reduce the economic costs of operating such an airport. The technical conditions of virtual tower operation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Development of air transport in two key regions in the Slovak Republic with regard to their character
abstract: The paper deals with the topic of air transport development in two key regions in the Slovak Republic with regard to their character. The paper contains a description of the current state of air transport in the Slovak Republic and the individual attributes of the air transport market. Two catchment areas of international Slovak airports - Milan Rastislav Štefánik Airport Bratislava and Košice International Airport, individual elements of these catchment areas and competing airports are characterized. An important factor is the impact of air transport on the development of the regions in relation to industry and tourism, where it addresses the direct, indirect induced and catalytic economic effects of air transport on the region. The role of industry and tourism in the region in relation to air transport is crucial. The intention was to define specific proposals for the development of air transport in selected regions and their connection to industry and tourism. The proposals presented in the paper for the development of air transport should lead to the attractiveness of the air transport in the given regions and contribute to the increase of the number of passengers who could use air transport. Proposals for the development of air transport are processed based on the results of the questionnaire of tourism and industry.

articleTitle: Displaying Additive Information in the Pilot’s Visual Field Using Augmented Reality Glasses
abstract: Ergonomically appropriate placement of flight instruments reduces the crew’s workload and reduces the likelihood of misinterpretation of displayed information. There are established instrument layout standards adapted by aircraft manufacturers that allow pilots to more easily transition from one aircraft to another. However, in certain phases of the flight, increased attention of the crew to the external environment is required. However, the instruments are located on the dashboard and the pilot must still switch between the instruments and the view from the cockpit. This problem is partially solved by the Head-mounted display located in front of the windshield. It is thus possible to follow the displayed information while looking ahead. In this respect, the existing Head-mounted display technology could be surpassed by technology implementing augmented reality into glasses (in some cases into a helmet) as a head/helmet-mounted display. The aim of this article is therefore to design an instrument layout for head-mounted devices. An important part is the conducted pilot testing and evaluation of feedback, which was evaluated using a questionnaire survey. The results point to the possibilities of flight information presentation, which could be configured within the possibilities of the available software and at the same time meet the ergonomic concepts and requirements of the pilots.

articleTitle: Grant Financing in Transport Sector in Slovakia
abstract: The transport sector contributes 14% to the creation of the gross domestic product of the Slovak Republic. The paper examines the issue of funding sources for its further development in the context of new social and technological challenges. Using the method of historical and content analysis of data, it finds answers to research questions and generalization of knowledge that can be used in practice. Grant financing in transport sector in Slovakia is almost totally European Union (EU) dependent. During three programming periods generous EU allocations supported transport enormously. However, this situation is not sustainable in the long run. It is time now to look for alternatives.

articleTitle: Intelligent airport protection supported by sophisticated security systems
abstract: Critical infrastructure defined as that part of the national infrastructure, the destruction or malfunctioning of which due to the action of a risk factor will cause a threat or disruption of the political and economic functioning of the state or a threat to the life and health of the population. As an element of critical infrastructure, the airport is obliged to maintain its security at a sufficient level even in changing security, economic and social conditions. The protection of the airport as an element of critical infrastructure brings the requirements for securing the perimeter of the airport with a high standard security. The aim of the article, to focus on different technologies and try to approach the decision-making process when designing a solution for an airport.

articleTitle: Use Of HLFC Technology In Low-Speed Civil Aviation Applications
abstract: With technological developments and the constant demand for increased safety and efficiency, transport, and aviation, in particular, is one of the most modern sectors of technology. Optimization of known principles is now an essential part of the modernization of aviation technology. The presented manuscript explores the implementation of Hybrid Laminar Flow Control technology, which is to this moment used in airliners only, in the small sport flying sector for significant optimization. The use of a low-speed wind tunnel allowed to verify the established hypothesis and to experimentally validate the proposed modifications of the HLFC technology within the framework of possible integration into the world of “general aviation”. The results of the experiments showed the potential and application in small-scale flying both in terms of increasing flight safety and optimizing the use of aerodynamic elements in order to reduce fuel consumption and flight efficiency.
